items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern digital redraw of a historical script form
items.caption: A modern redraw of 天 in Shuowen seal-script style. The earlier head-marked human-figure interpretation is supported by paleographic accounts, but this later form alone does not establish whether “head/top” or “sky” was the earliest spoken meaning.
items.alt: Modern vector rendering of the character 天 in a seal-script style, as identified by the Commons file page; pixels not independently inspected in this research.
items.selection_reason: The failed oracle-script file is replaced with this separately verified, reusable Tian form. It provides an attested later script tradition relevant to the graph's history; its caption avoids treating the redraw as an ancient artifact or as proof of a disputed semantic sequence.
items.rights: The Commons description page states CC0 1.0 and attributes a source image to Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang; the page also notes a Richard Sears source agreement for other material. The selected file's page explicitly makes this vector available under CC0 1.0.

limitations.text: The image is a modern vector redraw of a Shuowen seal-script form, not a photograph of a dated inscription. The direct SVG could not be rendered by the web tool; its provenance and rights were verified from the exact Commons description page, but its pixels were not independently inspected.
The head-marked analysis and the competing sky-first account do not establish one certain earliest spoken sense or a complete head/top-to-sky semantic chronology.
